chunks: From him, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Hariz ibn Abdullah, from Zurarah, who said:

I said to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him): A man recited a chapter in one bowing (rak'ah) and made a mistake; should he leave the place where he made the mistake and continue in his recitation, or leave that chapter and switch to another? He said: 'All of that is permissible, and if he recited a single verse and wished to bow with it, he bows.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is applicable to the voluntary prayer, for we have clarified that in the obligatory prayer it is not permissible to have less than a chapter along with the Opening (Al-Hamd).

key_terms.رَكْعَةٍ: A single unit of bowing in prayer

ai.seo_question: What should a Muslim do if they make a mistake while reciting a Quranic chapter during prayer?
ai.summary: This narration from Zurara to Imam al-Baqir clarifies the flexibility in recitation errors, permitting the worshipper to either continue from the mistake or switch chapters, a ruling derived by scholars like Muhammad ibn al-Hasan to apply primarily to voluntary (Nafil) prayers. This distinction highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that while obligatory prayers strictly require Surah Al-Fatiha plus another full chapter, voluntary prayers allow for greater leniency and adaptability in recitation structure. The hadith underscores the practical ease granted in personal devotion, contrasting with the stricter structural requirements of the five daily prayers.
